newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir turned to face sun to help boost power - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Mir turned to face sun to help boost power - Tass.

text.p: Russian cosmonauts have turned their damaged Mir space station to face the sun to help boost power supplies after a cargo craft collided with one of its science units, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.

Reporting from Mission Control near Moscow, Tass also said the Spektr science module's cooling system may have been broken in Wednesday's accident. Officials said the men on board, two Russians and an American, were in no immediate danger.
"The crew on board Mir changed its position back to face the sun to supply the necessary boost to the electrical supply's buffer batteries after the accident," the agency said.
In Wednesday's collision, an unmanned Progress cargo craft bumped into the Spektr module, damaging one of four solar panels and robbing the entire station of up to half its energy supply.
Tass said the cooling system in that part of the station, now sealed off from the rest of the sprawling complex to stop a drop in air pressure, could also be damaged.

Russian officials said late on Wednesday the crew may have to go on an unscheduled space walk to inspect the damage caused in the incident, described by Mission Control as one of the worst Mir has experienced in the 11 years it has been in orbit.
